definition: An annual income tax return filed by a corporation that has elected to be taxed as an S corporation, reporting the corporation's income, deductions, and credits, with income and deductions passed through to shareholders via separate statements.

includes.text: Form reports income and deductions for an S corporation with pass-through taxation to shareholders
Form includes detailed schedules for reporting shareholder allocations and basis adjustments
Form reports ordinary business income or loss from operations

excludes.text: A C corporation return that does not pass income through to shareholders but instead reports corporate-level tax
An amended individual return filed to correct a prior year's tax liability
An information return reporting dividends paid to shareholders rather than the corporation's own income

discriminators.text: This form passes through income and deductions to multiple shareholders via separate statements; the sibling is a corporate-level return where the corporation itself pays tax on all income
This is an original return for the current tax year; the sibling is an amended return filed to correct a prior year
This is a tax return reporting the corporation's business operations and income; the sibling is an information return reporting distributions of dividends to recipients
